## Why visit

The ceramic bar front makes this a must-see for anyone who enjoys pub architecture. It is a small, atmospheric pub where the decorative counter and old bar fittings deserve as much attention as the beer. Robinsons cask roots add a regional dimension, while the music room gives the building a living purpose beyond heritage tourism. Visit earlier if you want to examine the room quietly, or check the programme if an intimate gig would make the evening more interesting.

## Beer

CAMRA documents Robinsons cask ales with guest handpumps; regular names include Unicorn, Dizzy Blonde and Trooper, without guaranteeing the day’s lineup.

## Plan the visit

Check gig listings and any ticket requirements separately from pub access. The front room has a jukebox; this is also a functioning music pub.

**Getting there:** Walk along Oldham Street from Piccadilly Gardens or the Northern Quarter; pairs with Port Street Beer House.
